description: Distilled schematic and PCB skill gates derived from the provided skill pack. These rules are evidence-triggered review gates for local document generation.

gates.title: Schematic Topology And Operating Point Review
gates.objective: Confirm the schematic is electrically coherent before simulation or release documentation.
checklist: Confirm every power pin is driven by a named rail.
Check for floating high-impedance nodes and missing bias paths.
Confirm outputs are not fighting other outputs.
Create an operating-point table for rails and key control signals.
Mark every unknown voltage/current value as evidence required.

gates.title: PCB Physics Review
gates.objective: Convert schematic findings into physical PCB risk checks for geometry, copper, thermal, and cost.
checklist: Check DC power integrity and expected IR drop per rail.
Identify controlled-impedance and differential-pair nets.
Flag thermal hotspots around regulators, FETs, modem power, and fan output.
Check connector orientation, mounting, and mechanical stress points.
Record weakest assumptions that require CAD, Gerber, or measurement evidence.

gates.title: Power Integrity And PDN Gate
gates.objective: Verify the board can deliver clean, stable, low-impedance power to all consumers.
checklist: Build a rail budget with idle, typical, peak, and fault current.
Define target impedance from allowed ripple and transient current.
Use bulk, mid, high-frequency, and very-high-frequency decoupling tiers where needed.
Require local 100 nF decoupling close to every VCC pin where CAD evidence is available.
Keep DC rail droop below 2 percent at critical consumers.

gates.title: Signal Integrity Gate
gates.objective: Protect high-speed interfaces from reflections, skew, return-path detours, and crosstalk.
checklist: Assign impedance targets per high-speed interface.
Check continuous reference plane and stitching vias at layer transitions.
Verify differential-pair polarity and length matching against interface requirements.
Avoid long stubs and uncontrolled branches.
Plan TDR, eye, or packet-level validation for fast links.

gates.title: EMI/EMC External Port Gate
gates.objective: Reduce emissions and improve immunity before pre-compliance testing.
checklist: Place protection/filtering at every external connector or cable entry.
Minimize switching and cable loop areas.
Avoid routing high-speed signals across plane splits.
Define shield and chassis ground strategy.
Target at least 6 dB margin in pre-compliance scans.

gates.title: Protection Cascade Gate
gates.objective: Ensure external ports have coordinated ESD, surge, over-voltage, and filter strategy.
checklist: Create a threat model per port: ESD, EFT, surge, cable fault, and repetition.
Use coarse, medium, and fine protection stages where the energy level requires it.
Keep clamp return paths short, wide, and routed to the correct ground reference.
Confirm TVS capacitance is compatible with the protected signal speed.
Document fuse and protection coordination for fault events.

gates.title: Design For Testability Gate
gates.objective: Make the board testable at prototype, production, and field-service stages.
checklist: Add test access for every rail, ground, reset, boot, and critical interface signal.
Plan SWD/JTAG/UART programming or debug access.
Define ICT/flying-probe and functional test coverage targets.
Use diagnostic LEDs or telemetry where useful.
Record serial number, station, operator, measurements, and result traceability.

gates.title: PCB Test Hierarchy Gate
gates.objective: Turn generated documentation into a layered validation and production test plan.
checklist: Start with visual inspection and pre-power continuity.
Use current-limited power-up and verify every named rail.
Test clocks, boot, firmware programming, and debug path.
Run one simplest transaction on every interface.
Feed field failures back into the test plan.

gates.title: Design For Manufacturability Gate
gates.objective: Keep the board inside the selected fabricator capability tier and avoid avoidable yield loss.
checklist: Confirm target fabricator capability before layout release.
Match DRC to trace, space, drill, annular ring, mask, and copper rules.
Specify stackup, copper weight, finish, impedance table, via fill, and panelization.
Add fiducials and test coupons where production requires them.
Use fabricator DFM review before ordering.

gates.title: Thermal Reliability Gate
gates.objective: Protect component life by budgeting dissipation and validating junction temperature.
checklist: Estimate per-component dissipation for regulators, FETs, modem power, and fan drivers.
Keep junction temperature below 80 percent of absolute maximum at worst ambient.
Use copper spreading, thermal vias, heatsink, or airflow where needed.
Separate heat sources from sensitive analog/RF parts.
Validate with thermal camera or contact measurements.

gates.title: Supply Chain And BOM Gate
gates.objective: Treat every extracted key part as a supply-chain risk object before procurement.
checklist: Confirm lifecycle status: Active, NRND, LTB, EOL, or Obsolete.
Identify at least one qualified alternate for critical parts.
Check stock, lead time, MOQ, package, and grade.
Avoid grey-market sources unless counterfeit screening is specified.
Maintain an approved vendor list tied to board revision.

gates.title: Wireless/RF Certification Gate
gates.objective: Separate radio connectivity from release claims that require antenna, carrier, RF, and regional evidence.
checklist: Confirm approved antenna, RF path, SIM ESD, modem supply, and reset/enable lines.
Document regional certification and carrier requirements.
Validate network registration, GNSS, UART/USB data, and status indicators.
Keep antenna and RF layout constraints separate from ordinary digital routing.
Record RF exposure and enclosure assumptions.

gates.title: Isolation, Creepage, And Clearance Gate
gates.objective: Prevent safety documentation from claiming release readiness without spacing and insulation evidence.
checklist: Identify hazardous voltage domains and protective earth strategy.
Verify creepage and clearance against the product standard and pollution degree.
Confirm slots, barriers, opto/isolator ratings, and transformer insulation class.
Separate primary, secondary, SELV, chassis, and signal ground references.
Require lab safety evidence before customer-facing compliance claims.
